LESSON: KENYAN INDIGENOUS MUSICAL INSTRUMENT (SOLO PERFORMANCE)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.3: Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instrument (Solo Performance)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instrument (Solo Performance), part of Performing in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How is proficiency in solo instrumental playing developed? 2. How do we identify features of a solo instrument that mark its cultural identity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instrument (Solo Performance) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication: The learner listens critically and speaks clearly while giving feedback on peers’ performances.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner uses imagination to improvise and play melodies/rhythms on an

instrument(s).

● Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital devices to search for the techniques of tuning, playing and

maintaining various instruments.

Values:
● Integrity: The learner uses the internet appropriately when searching for tech play.

● Responsibility: The learner uses learning resources with utmost care.

● Respect: The learner respects others’ views during rehearsal sessions of the Western instrument.

● Social Justice: The learner is given an equal opportunity to play tunes from diverse Kenyan communities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Resource mobilization: The learner sources for music from the internet and other sources for music to play.

● Mentorship: The learner interacts with resource persons to learn the techniques of tuning, playing and

maintaining the instruments.

40

Suggested Learning Resources

● A variety of Indigenous Kenyan musical instrument (Aerophones, Idiophones, Chordophones and

Membranophones).

● Digital devices with appropriate assistive technology.

● Resource persons.

● Braille equipment and materials.

● Exercise books in appropriate print.

● Textbook in print and in braille.

● Audio visual recordings of instrumental performances.

Suggested Key Skills to be Assessed

● Explaining sound production on a selected Kenyan indigenous musical instrument.

● Performing music from the cultural idiom of the chosen instrument.
